title: RBI Holds Repo Rate Unchanged, Projects 6.9% GDP Growth Amid Crude Surge
summary: The RBI's rate hold arrives precisely as MCX Crude trades at ₹8,675/bbl, up 3.02% on the session, creating a direct macro tension. An unchanged repo rate preserves rupee carry dynamics at USD/INR ₹95.27, but a sustained crude rally structurally widens India's import bill, pressuring the current account and introducing latent INR depreciation risk. The import parity chain runs as follows: every dollar rise in Brent translates to approximately ₹95.27 per barrel of additional landed cost at current FX, compounding the crude rally's domestic impact. The 6.9% GDP projection sustains industrial demand assumptions for MCX Copper, currently at ₹1,314.40/kg despite today's 1.00% decline. MCX Gold at ₹1,47,946/10g faces competing forces: a rate hold is historically supportive of gold, while risk-on energy sentiment historically compresses safe-haven premiums. The confirmation level to watch is the next WTI settlement relative to the ₹90/bbl crude import parity threshold for RBI's fiscal math.

title: MCX Gold slides 2.95% to ₹147,946 as energy surge redirects risk capital away from metal
summary: The mechanism here is capital rotation, not fundamental gold weakness. Crude's 3.02% surge to ₹8,675/bbl signals supply-shock pricing, historically pulling speculative flows toward energy and compressing gold's relative appeal within the same commodity allocation pool. Import parity arithmetic: spot gold near $3,105/oz × ₹95.27 × 1.155 duty factor = theoretical MCX parity approximately ₹153,200/10g — placing current MCX at roughly a ₹5,250 discount to parity, a structural observation traders historically monitor for mean reversion signals. Silver at ₹2,36,300/kg is also down, confirming broad metals pressure rather than gold-specific selling. Copper's 1.00% decline further validates the metals-off positioning. Key support observed at ₹146,500; resistance at ₹150,200. Watch tomorrow's US CPI release — historically the single scheduled catalyst capable of repricing gold's real-rate narrative at MCX open.

title: MCX Crude surges 3.02% to ₹8675/bbl as energy supply concerns grip global markets
summary: The mechanism: energy supply anxiety is driving simultaneous bids across crude and natural gas, with Brent-linked import parity pulling MCX Crude higher in lockstep.

title: MCX Gold slides 2.75% to ₹148,250 as crude-led risk rotation pressures safe-haven demand
summary: The mechanism here is risk-appetite rotation. Crude's +3.1% surge signals markets pricing geopolitical risk through energy rather than safe-haven metals — capital is moving toward the supply-disruption trade, not the uncertainty hedge. That rotation pulls institutional money away from gold positions this session.

title: MCX Crude surges 3.10% to ₹8682/bbl as energy complex leads commodity session
summary: The 3.10% crude advance reflects a risk-on energy bid, with supply-side compression mechanics — historically, sessions where crude leads the complex by this magnitude show institutional rotation out of defensive metals into energy contracts. MCX Gold at ₹148250 and Silver at ₹235844 confirm capital rotation, each under pressure.
